newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Avesta Sheffield scrapes profit in 6 mo 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Avesta Sheffield scrapes profit in 6 mo 1996/97.

text.p: Swedish/British steel producer Avesta Sheffield said on Friday that its profits for the first six months of 1996/97 were almost wiped out by low prices and losses in inventories.

The company said current chief executive officer Per Molin would step down in June 1997 to be replaced by Stuart Pettifor, currently president of the sections, plates, and commercial steel division of parent company British Steel.
Avesta posted a pre-tax profit for the six months to September 30 of just 24 million crowns compared to 2.29 billion crowns in the same period a year ago.
This was below market expectations with analysts expecting a pre-tax profit of 169 million crowns.
"A loss in the second quarter of 204 million crowns was caused by lower sales prices and losses in inventories of 182 million crowns," the company said in a statement.
Sales during the six months tumbled 25 percent to 8.42 billion crowns.
"The strengthening of the Swedish crown cut the result by about 100 million crowns compared with 1995/96," said Avesta Sheffield.
"Internally, problems with the commissioning and work up of new equipment at Avesta melt shop, Nyby cold mill and Baltimore CMP line have also had a negative impact," Avesta said.
But the company said all these developments were performing much better by the end of the period.
Avesta said price rises announced for coil products that reached an exceptionally low point in July/August this syear, have been effective.
"The price rises will provide some modest recovery in profitability," it said.
"Further increases are expected but it is uncertain at what pace they will be achieved.
"The group, rather than relying on improving external conditions is putting priority focus on measurres to improve cost efficiency and realise the full benefits of its completed investments."
On the world market for stainless steel, Avesta said international production fell by 1.5 percent in the first half of 1996 against a year ago and in Europe by five percent.

For cold rolled sheet, Avesta's most important product group, deliveries into the European market by European producers were around one million tonnes which was about 12 percent lower than a year ago.
"Such a fall in volume was the natural consequence of the stock build which has now been progressively reversed," the company said.
"The group judges that stocks are now nearing a level consistent with real demand."
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 6.618 Swedish Crowns)
